name: Revolut
look: Two-mode canvas switched in full-bleed bands, a white pill as the brightest pixel, and eight accents confined to product mockups.

hero.title: Money without the friction
hero.sub: Spend in thirty-six currencies at the real exchange rate, split a bill in a tap, and see where it went without exporting a statement.

features.title: Everything in one place
features.sub: The accounts, cards and transfers you would otherwise hold at four institutions.

items.title: 36 currencies
items.body: Hold and spend at the interbank rate, with the markup shown rather than hidden in the rate.

items.title: Instant transfers
items.body: Between accounts instantly and free; internationally in seconds with the fee stated first.

items.title: Spending insight
items.body: Categorised automatically, with monthly budgets that actually nudge before you overspend.

items.title: Disposable cards
items.body: A single-use virtual card for the subscription you suspect you will want to cancel.

items.title: Savings vaults
items.body: Round up spare change or set a schedule, with the interest rate stated plainly.

items.title: Freeze in a tap
items.body: Lose a card and freeze it instantly; unfreeze when it turns up in a coat pocket.

showcases.title: The markup, not just the rate
showcases.body: Everyone claims a good exchange rate. We show the interbank rate and our markup as separate numbers, so the comparison is possible rather than rhetorical.
points: Interbank rate and markup shown separately
Fee-free allowance shown as you use it

showcases.title: For companies with the same problem
showcases.body: Multi-currency accounts, cards with per-person limits, and expense capture that does not require anyone to photograph a receipt in a taxi.
points: Expenses captured at the point of spend

gallery.title: THE APP
gallery.sub: What it looks like in the hand.

testimonial.quote: I moved abroad and stopped thinking about currency entirely. The bit that surprised me was seeing the markup as a separate line rather than buried in the rate.
testimonial.name: Ana Ribeiro

pricing.title: PLANS
pricing.sub: Free to start. Paid tiers raise the fee-free allowances.

items.q: What is the real exchange rate?
items.a: The interbank rate, shown alongside our markup as a separate figure. Above your fee-free allowance the markup applies; below it, it does not.
Deposits are held at partner banks under the relevant protection scheme in your country, and the specific scheme and limit are stated on the account page.
Currency markets close, so a small weekend surcharge applies on exchanges. It is shown before you confirm rather than discovered on the statement.

items.q: Can I use it as my main account?
items.a: Yes — salary can be paid in, direct debits are supported, and the account details are your own rather than pooled.

cta.title: Get started in minutes
cta.sub: Free to open, and you can see the markup before you convert anything.

notes: Two canvas modes switched in full-bleed bands: true black for storytelling, white for browsing. Never blended in one section.
Display type runs tight — line-height 1.0 with heavy negative tracking at large sizes.
The actual primary CTA is a white pill with black text on the dark canvas, deliberately the brightest pixel. The brand violet is for featured plan cards and secondary actions.
Eight saturated accents live inside product mockups and illustrations only. None of them is ever a button surface.
All buttons are pills, content cards take a generous 20px, and inputs and chips step down to 12px.
